name: Pi
invoke: run the role as its own pi session — `pi -p "$(waypost agents show <role>) <target>"`
roles_note: Pi ships no sub-agents: its README says so outright and points at extensions instead, so there is no directory a role file would be read from. A role is a separate pi session, which is what these roles need anyway — a fresh context.

skills.notes: Walks the working directory and its ancestors up to the repo root; on a name collision the first skill found wins.

notes: A deliberately minimal harness: four tools (Read, Write, Edit, Bash) and everything else added at runtime as extensions, skills and packages. It reads AGENTS.md walking up from the working directory (also CLAUDE.md, and ~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md globally), so `waypost agents register` reaches it — but note that a directory holding AGENTS.override.md is loaded INSTEAD of AGENTS.md there, which would hide the routing block; .pi/SYSTEM.md likewise replaces the system prompt. Detection is by .pi/, and the env markers are real ones the harness sets for its children (PI_CODING_AGENT, PI_SESSION_ID), so a commit from pi labels itself without WAYPOST_HARNESS. If you install the third-party pi-subagents package (`pi install npm:@tintinweb/pi-subagents`), agent types DO become files — .pi/agents/<name>.md, or the shared .agents/agents/<name>.md — and this entry is worth overriding in .waypost/harnesses/pi.json with: {"id":"pi","detect":[".pi"],"instructions":["AGENTS.md"],"invoke":"delegate to the `waypost-<role>` subagent","roles":{"shape":"frontmatter-md","dir":".pi/agents","file":"{prefix}{role}.md","model":{"tiers":{}},"fields":[["name","{prefix}{role}"],["description","{description}"],["model","{model}"]]}}. Leave `tools` out of that override: pi's vocabulary is not Claude's (no Grep or Glob — grep is Bash), and an allowlist written from a guess strips what the role needs. The bundled entry stays `none` because that is what stock pi is.
